classification.difficultyReason: Use logarithms to find a compound-interest threshold, then select and verify the first whole year.

content.prompt: An amount of $\$120\,000$ is invested on 1 Jan at a compound interest rate of $8\%$ per annum. Interest is only paid on 1 Jan of each year. At the end of how many years will the investment first be worth at least:

answer.worked:
Let $A_n$ be the value after $n$ years.

$$\begin{align*}A_n&=120\,000(1.08)^n\\160\,000&=120\,000(1.08)^n\\\frac43&=(1.08)^n\\\log_{10}\left(\frac43\right)&=n\log_{10}(1.08)\\n&=\frac{\log_{10}(4/3)}{\log_{10}(1.08)}\\n&=3.738022\ldots\end{align*}$$

Interest is paid annually, so check the adjacent whole years:

$$\begin{align*}A_3&=120\,000(1.08)^3=151\,165.44\\A_4&=120\,000(1.08)^4\approx163\,258.68\end{align*}$$

The investment first reaches at least $\$160\,000$ after 4 years.

Let $A_n$ be the value after $n$ years.

$$\begin{align*}A_n&=120\,000(1.08)^n\\200\,000&=120\,000(1.08)^n\\\frac53&=(1.08)^n\\\log_{10}\left(\frac53\right)&=n\log_{10}(1.08)\\n&=\frac{\log_{10}(5/3)}{\log_{10}(1.08)}\\n&=6.637457\ldots\end{align*}$$

Interest is paid annually, so check the adjacent whole years:

$$\begin{align*}A_6&=120\,000(1.08)^6\approx190\,424.92\\A_7&=120\,000(1.08)^7\approx205\,658.91\end{align*}$$

The investment first reaches at least $\$200\,000$ after 7 years.
